category_title: Students with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) showing variable engagement
minimal_context: The student is working on a math worksheet at their desk while receiving one-on-one instruction from a teacher in a co-taught mainstream classroom.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Here is the math worksheet for today. Let's go through the first few problems together at your desk.

STUDENT: (Looks at the worksheet and starts writing the answers, keeping their head down and working alone.)

TUTOR: The students next to you are comparing their answers. You can talk to them.

STUDENT: (Continues to look only at the paper, showing no interaction behaviour with the peers nearby.)

TUTOR: Why don't you show them what you wrote for number two?

STUDENT: (Turns away from the peers to face the teacher completely, continuing to work alone and avoiding any interaction with the rest of the class.)

options.A: Provide written feedback using a 3-point scale after the math worksheet.
options.B: Incorporate frequent opportunities for the student to respond during math instruction.
options.C: Promote cooperative learning rather than preventing it during the math activity.
options.D: Provide a clear beginning and end for each math worksheet task.
